parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the ESM, manual argv, no external dependencies, bucketize, BigInt, and Python-style formatting requirements from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation and final delivery ownership while spawning probe and review children for executable behavior and final edge-case review.
parallel.implementation: It wrote a compact ESM module set, but parseArguments rejected separate --a values starting with '-' and parsePythonInt used an ASCII-only digit regex.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent assembled /output/test5.mjs with local modules and delivered the file set after local checks, with no completed review child handoff incorporated.
parallel.verification: It verified common success and argparse cases and one negative comma case, while the active reviewer was still exploring hidden integer compatibility cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The reviewer child found Python accepted non-ASCII decimal digits that the Node parser rejected, and the official result remained 142 of 144.

serial.requirements: The serial run worked from the same prompt and recognized the same ESM, CLI, int conversion, bucketize, output formatting, and no-dependency obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, patching, and final delivery without delegation or handoff lifecycle risk.
serial.implementation: It created a deeper module hierarchy and explicitly handled argparse negative-number value boundaries, then patched traceback footer formatting.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial agent assembled the entrypoint and local modules in /output and delivered the expected artifact set after its own checks.
serial.verification: It ran broad local parity checks including help, missing and unknown args, repeated --a, --a=, underscores, negative-number boundaries, and invalid integer failures.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task-relevant work is visible in the serial trajectory, and the official evaluator passed all 144 samples.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel understood the required CLI, int conversion, bucketize, formatting, ESM, and no-dependency constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and implemented the same required behavior in pure ESM modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The requirement understanding was broadly similar; the material difference was in how thoroughly edge-case CLI and int behavior was carried into implementation and closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used multiple children for probing and review while the parent retained implementation and final response ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no subagents and one agent owned probing, implementation, verification, and finalization.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel strategy introduced a reviewer lifecycle dependency, while the serial strategy kept all findings and fixes in one execution context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent explicitly delegated a final review pass after local behavior checks and before final handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not transfer task context across agents; edge-case observations stayed in the same thread that edited the code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created a parent-review child boundary whose result had to be joined; serial avoided that handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented local modules, but its CLI parser refused most separate --a values beginning with '-' and its int parser accepted only ASCII digits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial explicitly modeled argparse's negative-number boundary and later tightened error traceback formatting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial implemented and tested a value-boundary behavior that the parallel implementation left wrong; the reviewer also showed an unincorporated parallel integer-compatibility mismatch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited, saw review_output still running, marked the plan complete, and interrupted that active child before a review result returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed and used its own checks and patches before final delivery, with no child result to join.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closed while a needed review child was active; serial's result lifecycle remained local and complete before final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered a coherent file set with no proven write collision or overwrite among live agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered a coherent ESM file set with all modules owned by the same agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no material shared-state collision difference; the important difference is result lifecycle and verification depth rather than workspace overwrite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel local tests passed for selected cases, but the active reviewer then found integer behavior mismatches that were not folded into acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran additional parity checks and patched a remaining bad-integer traceback mismatch before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial kept checking and patching before closure; parallel closed after local checks despite an interrupted reviewer with active edge-case findings.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spent several waits on review_output, timed out, then closed by interrupting it rather than reallocating or taking over review findings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used its time for continued local probing, patching, and final checks and completed with no visible unfinished work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure cut off active review work; serial closure followed completed local verification and official pass.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluation is serial_only_pass: parallel scored 142 of 144 while serial scored 144 of 144. Pair-local evidence shows parallel shipped a parser that rejected separate --a values starting with '-' and closed while a review child was still actively investigating hidden integer compatibility; serial explicitly modeled argparse's negative-number value boundary, patched a remaining traceback mismatch, and completed all official samples. The pair does not expose per-case official failures, so this is a supported comparative explanation rather than a claim of a unique root cause.
parallel_contributors: Parallel parseArguments rejected negative-looking separate --a values because it treated a following token starting with '-' as missing.
Parallel interrupted review_output while it was actively testing integer edge cases and had demonstrated Python/Node mismatch evidence.
Parallel final acceptance listed local checks but did not incorporate the active reviewer findings before delivery.
serial_contributors: Serial explicitly identified argparse's negative-number value heuristic and implemented a matching canConsumeValue path.
Serial patched the PyInstaller traceback footer mismatch before finalizing.
Serial finished with official solution_passed true and 144 of 144 samples.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The parallel CLI parser was too broad in rejecting dash-prefixed values after --a, while serial handled negative integers and negative-looking invalid values more like argparse.
The child-discovered non-ASCII digit mismatch is a real parallel implementation gap, but the pair-local official summaries do not prove that exact gap accounts for the two official failures.
evaluator_effects: The official status files provide only aggregate counts, not the individual failed cases.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The parallel parent owned implementation and wrote the required /output ESM files, so implementation ownership was not absent.
The parent assembled its own modules into test5.mjs; no separately owned components lacked an integration owner.
The parent created the final entrypoint and delivered the file set, so final assembly ownership existed.
The parent managed implementation, checks, final delivery, and child interactions; the issue was a premature child stop, not an unowned pipeline.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent implemented and tested while probes and review work were used as support.
The parallel run did not complete all investigation as a separate first phase before implementation; investigation, implementation, and review overlapped.
The indispensable implementation path had an active parent owner and produced a deliverable; the adverse event is the later reviewer interruption, not capacity starvation.
Although several children existed, the record does not show collective fan-out exhausting the run budget; the parent chose to interrupt one active review child.
The review task was not proven overbroad relative to available time; it was actively producing edge-case evidence when the parent interrupted it.
The review child understood it should inspect constraints and hidden edge cases; the loss came from interruption before final return, not an omitted initial requirement.
No separately owned implementation components had incompatible file, export, input, or output contracts requiring reconciliation.
No known finding is shown disappearing through a summary or compaction transfer; the reviewer result was never finalized because the child was interrupted.
There was no large completed handoff containing needed information that the parent failed to reduce within the decision window.
No parent or child acted on a superseded handoff; the relevant review information was actively being generated when interrupted.
The record does not show incompatible completed reports reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated.
The parent had local end-to-end checks; the hidden official failure and unreturned child work do not by themselves establish a parent-visible integrated acceptance gap.
There is no replacement or retry agent that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent spawned review_output, observed it running after waits, marked its own plan complete, and explicitly interrupted that active child while it was testing hidden int compatibility and had demonstrated mismatches. Correction required waiting for the reviewer, retrieving its result, or taking over the discovered compatibility work before final delivery.
candidates.realized_consequence: The active reviewer did not return a final review and its discovered integer-compatibility evidence was not incorporated before the parent delivered a solution that failed the official evaluator.
candidates.near_match_reason: A verifier finding existed inside the child, but the parent explicitly interrupted the child while running; the direct lifecycle error is premature termination rather than a completed verifier result trapped below the parent.

candidates.reason: No complete corrected candidate containing the review child's fixes was available and simply left unpromoted; the child work was unfinished because it was interrupted.
No child result or implementation change was merged after integrated verification; the active review result was never returned or merged.
No completed delegated implementation was available and left unretrieved; the relevant child was a reviewer, not an implementation owner.
The review child had findings in its own trajectory but did not complete a final verifier return; the parent interrupted it while still running, making Early Child Termination more specific.
The child cancellation is the same lifecycle chain as the retained early termination, and the parent caused the stop rather than reacting to an independent child failure.
The relevant review_output child did not provide a completed result that was visible to the parent and ignored.
The parent did wait through timeouts, but it also listed and interacted with the child; the directly corrective boundary is the later explicit interruption.
No competing concurrent file sets with incompatible ownership were integrated or required reconciliation in the submitted output.
There is no direct evidence that two live agents edited the same source file and one had to reconcile the other's concurrent change.
No non-entry module produced or owned by another agent is shown being replaced, deleted, or wholesale rewritten by a different live actor.
The required entrypoint was delivered by the parent; no concurrent overwrite of the submitted deliverable by another owner is proven.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final outputs and invalidated another actor's final-tree work.
Shared workspace use did not produce a concrete unstable-state or provenance problem beyond the retained interrupted review lifecycle.
No generated artifact, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed as misleading stable input by another actor.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The parent spawned review_output for final review, saw it still running, declared all local work complete, and interrupted it while it was actively checking hidden int compatibility and had produced mismatch evidence. The proper coordination boundary was to join that review or take over its findings before final delivery.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: A live review branch with concrete edge-case mismatch evidence was cut off, leaving that review unreturned and unincorporated before a failing official parallel delivery.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The child did not finish and return a verifier result that got trapped; the parent explicitly stopped the active child, so Early Child Termination is the more direct label.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Missing Verifier Return, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered for the same review_output chain but suppressed because the explicit active-child interruption is the directly corrective boundary.
